blocks.text: The two officers had previously been placed on administrative leave and then fired from the Montreal police service. They were arrested after Quebec's Crown prosecutor's office, the DPCP, issued a warrant.
Arrests connected to allegations of discriminatory, racist acts by officers at Station 39

The Service de police de la Ville de Montréal (SPVM) announced Saturday in a news release that it arrested two of its own officers in connection with allegations of discriminatory and racist acts by police officers at Station 39.
The arrested officers were released under the promise to return to court, where they will face charges of assault, criminal harassment and breach of trust, according to the SPVM.
The two officers had previously been placed on administrative leave, and were among seven police officers who were fired on Nov. 2.
Other related criminal investigations are still being handled by the SPVM's Division des normes professionnelles.
